name: Hash Map Complement Lookup
triggers: Need to find whether a matching value was seen before.
Input is unsorted or sorting would destroy required output info.
Need original indices or prior values.
invariant: map[value] = index of a value already seen.
failureModes: Sorting when original indices matter.
Adding current value before checking complement and accidentally using the same element twice.
Using a plain object instead of Map when keys could be numeric or collide with object prototype.
contrastCases: Two Sum II: input is already sorted, so two pointers are valid.
3Sum: sort + fixed anchor + two pointers is better because output is values/triplets, not original indices.

name: Frequency Map / Count Array
triggers: Need counts of values or characters.
Need to compare multiplicity, not just existence.
Key space may be fixed, like lowercase English letters.
invariant: count[x] = number of unmatched occurrences of x.
failureModes: Using a Set when duplicates/counts matter.
Assuming alphabet size without checking constraints.
Using a plain object as a frequency map and hitting prototype-key collisions on unusual inputs.
contrastCases: Contains Duplicate: pure existence check — a Set is enough; no counts needed.
Group Anagrams: need the frequency as a canonical key, not just a count comparison.

name: Two Pointers on Sorted Input
triggers: Input is sorted, or sorting is allowed.
Need pair/triplet relation like sum.
Moving one pointer has a monotonic effect.
whatItGives: O(n) scan after sorting or on already sorted input.
invariant: Current search space is between left and right. If sum is too small, move left. If sum is too large, move right.
failureModes: Using two pointers on unsorted input without monotonicity.
Sorting when original indices matter.
Incorrect duplicate skipping in 3Sum.
contrastCases: Two Sum: input is unsorted and you need original indices — use hash map instead.
Valid Palindrome: not sorted but still uses opposite-end convergence; non-alphanumeric skip complicates the loop.

name: Sliding Window
triggers: Need best/valid contiguous subarray or substring.
Window validity can be updated incrementally.
Moving left can restore validity.
whatItGives: Usually O(n) because each pointer moves at most n times.
invariant: The current window satisfies the validity condition before updating answer.
failureModes: Updating answer before restoring validity.
Forgetting why nested while is still O(n): each pointer only moves forward.
Using final window state instead of global best.
contrastCases: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock: single-pass greedy with implicit window — no explicit left/right shrink needed.
Frequency Map: counts chars but doesn't maintain a window boundary.

name: BFS Queue
triggers: Need shortest path in unweighted graph.
Need level order traversal.
Need to process nodes by distance/layers.
whatItGives: Processes nodes in breadth-first order; guarantees shortest path in unweighted graphs.
invariant: Queue contains discovered nodes whose neighbors have not been processed yet. Mark visited when enqueuing, not when dequeuing.
failureModes: Marking visited on dequeue, allowing duplicate queue entries.
Queueing metadata instead of node labels.
Confusing graph node set with edge list.
contrastCases: DFS: explores one branch fully before backtracking — does not guarantee shortest path.
Level Order Traversal: snapshot queue length at start of each level to group nodes.

name: DFS Cycle Detection
triggers: Directed graph.
Need to know if a dependency cycle exists.
Shared subgraphs can be reused after proven safe.
whatItGives: Detects cycles in directed graphs using three-color DFS; also used for topological sort.
invariant: 0 = unseen, 1 = visiting / current recursion path, 2 = done / proven safe. Seeing state 1 means cycle.
failureModes: Using boolean visited for directed cycle detection.
Not distinguishing currently visiting from fully processed.
Building graph from edge list incorrectly.
contrastCases: BFS for cycle detection: works for undirected graphs but not directed.
Topological sort (Kahn's): BFS-based alternative using in-degree counts.

name: Set Membership
triggers: Question is pure existence: has anything repeated or appeared?
No counts needed — only presence/absence matters.
Need O(1) lookup for prior elements.
whatItGives: O(1) average membership test with minimal overhead.
invariant: set contains all previously seen values; membership test answers 'was this seen before?'
failureModes: Using a frequency map when only existence is needed.
Sorting to detect duplicates when O(n) Set solution suffices.
contrastCases: Frequency Map: use when counts matter, not just presence.
Hash Map Complement: use when you need to find a matching pair, not just any duplicate.

name: Canonical Key Grouping
triggers: Need to group elements that share some equivalence relation.
Two elements are equivalent if their sorted form or frequency signature matches.
Output is groups, not individual matches.
whatItGives: Groups equivalents in one pass using a derived canonical key.
invariant: All elements with the same canonical key map to the same bucket.
failureModes: Using sorted string as key without considering Unicode edge cases.
Building frequency array key with join separator that can collide across character positions.
contrastCases: Frequency Map: compares two strings directly; Canonical Key Grouping groups many strings.
Set Membership: checks existence; Canonical Key Grouping produces grouped output.

name: Stack for Matching / Monotonic State
triggers: Need to match open/close pairs or nested structures.
Need to track the most recent unmatched element.
Monotonic property: answer depends on nearest larger/smaller element.
whatItGives: O(n) processing of nested or monotonic relationships.
invariant: Stack top is the most recent unmatched or relevant element; pop when a match or dominance condition is met.
failureModes: Popping without checking if stack is empty.
Forgetting to verify stack is empty at the end.
Using a queue instead of a stack (FIFO vs LIFO).
contrastCases: BFS Queue: FIFO; use for level-order traversal, not matching.
Min Stack: augmented stack for O(1) min queries — different from matching.

name: Tree DFS (Recursive)
triggers: Problem on a binary tree that can be solved per-node.
Answer at a node depends on answers from children (post-order) or parent context (pre-order).
Structural mutation or comparison of subtrees.
whatItGives: O(n) traversal with natural recursion; base case handles null nodes.
invariant: Each call returns the answer for its subtree; null returns the base-case value (0, true, null).
failureModes: Forgetting the null base case.
Confusing pre-order vs post-order when mutation order matters.
Returning a value that mixes subtree info with accumulated state.
contrastCases: BFS Queue: use when you need level-by-level processing, not depth-first.
Iterative DFS with explicit stack: needed when call-stack depth is a concern.

name: Grid DFS / BFS Flood Fill
triggers: Grid of cells; need to count or process connected components.
Need to mark all reachable cells from a starting cell.
Trigger phrase: 'connected component count in a grid'.
whatItGives: O(rows × cols) traversal of all connected cells.
invariant: Once a cell is visited (marked or set to '0'), it will not be counted again.
failureModes: Marking visited after processing instead of before, causing infinite recursion.
Forgetting bounds checks before array access.
Using BFS without a visited set for grids where mutation is not allowed.
contrastCases: Clone Graph: graph nodes, not grid cells — use adjacency list + visited map.
Tree DFS: tree has no cycles; grid may have 4-directional neighbors.

name: Prefix / Suffix Products
triggers: Need product of all elements except self.
No division allowed.
Answer at position i depends on all elements to its left and right.
whatItGives: O(n) solution without division by precomputing left and right running products.
invariant: result[i] = prefix[i] * suffix[i] where prefix[i] is product of all elements before i and suffix[i] is product of all elements after i.
failureModes: Trying to use division (fails when zeros are present).
Using O(n²) nested loop instead of prefix/suffix passes.
contrastCases: Running sum / prefix sum: for addition instead of multiplication.
Sliding window: for contiguous subarray problems, not element-exclusion products.

name: Heap / Top-K Selection
triggers: Need the K largest, K smallest, or K most frequent elements.
Need O(n log k) instead of O(n log n) full sort.
Problem mentions 'top K', 'K closest', or 'Kth largest'.
whatItGives: O(n log k) selection using a min-heap of size k.
invariant: Heap always contains the k best candidates seen so far; if new element beats the worst, replace it.
failureModes: Sorting the entire array when only K elements are needed.
Building a max-heap instead of min-heap for top-K (should evict the smallest).
contrastCases: Sort + slice: simpler but O(n log n); heap gives O(n log k).
QuickSelect: O(n) average for Kth element but harder to implement correctly.

name: Backtracking
triggers: Need all subsets, permutations, or combinations.
Build solution incrementally; abandon a branch when a constraint is violated.
Output is a list of complete paths through a decision tree.
whatItGives: Explores all valid paths in the decision tree; prunes invalid branches early.
invariant: At each recursive call, the current partial solution is valid; after the call returns, undo the last choice (backtrack).
failureModes: Forgetting to pop/undo after the recursive call (corrupts shared state).
Using the same start index for permutations (should allow revisiting positions).
Missing the base case for Combination Sum (target becomes 0 or negative).
contrastCases: DP: memoize overlapping subproblems; backtracking enumerates all solutions.
BFS: explores by distance; backtracking explores by decision depth.

name: 1-D Dynamic Programming
triggers: Optimal substructure: best answer for size n depends on best answers for smaller sizes.
Problem asks for count, min cost, or max value over a sequence.
Overlapping subproblems: naive recursion recomputes the same states.
whatItGives: O(n) bottom-up table fill after identifying the recurrence.
invariant: dp[i] holds the optimal answer for the first i elements (or up to position i); fill left to right.
failureModes: Off-by-one in the base case (dp[0] vs dp[1] meaning).
Using recursion without memoization, hitting exponential time.
Coin Change: forgetting to initialize dp with Infinity and handle unreachable states.
contrastCases: Backtracking: enumerates all paths; DP finds the optimal one.
Greedy: makes a local optimal choice; DP considers all subproblem outcomes.

name: Binary Search
triggers: Search space is sorted or has a monotonic property.
Can determine which half to discard at each step.
Problem asks for minimum feasible value (binary search on the answer).
whatItGives: O(log n) search by halving the search space each iteration.
invariant: Answer always lies within [left, right]; after each step the range shrinks by at least half.
failureModes: Integer overflow: use mid = left + Math.floor((right - left) / 2), not (left + right) / 2.
Off-by-one: confusing left <= right vs left < right termination conditions.
Rotated array: not checking which half is sorted before deciding where to search.
contrastCases: Two Pointers: both pointers move; binary search only moves one boundary per step.
Binary search on answer: search space is the value range, not array indices.

name: Linked List Traversal / Manipulation
triggers: Input is a singly linked list.
Need to reverse, merge, or restructure node pointers.
Two-pointer (fast/slow) technique for cycle or midpoint detection.
whatItGives: O(n) in-place manipulation by rearranging next pointers.
invariant: At each step, maintain the invariant about which nodes are fully processed; never lose a reference before re-pointing.
failureModes: Losing the next pointer before saving it during reversal.
Not using a dummy head node for merge, causing extra null checks.
Reorder List: not finding the midpoint correctly before reversing the second half.
contrastCases: Array two pointers: random access; linked list must traverse sequentially.
Tree DFS: tree is a linked structure but with two children, not one next pointer.

name: Graph Traversal (BFS/DFS on Adjacency List)
triggers: Input is a graph (not a tree, grid, or DAG for cycle detection).
Need to visit all reachable nodes from a source.
Need to clone, label, or count connected components in a general graph.
whatItGives: O(V + E) traversal of all reachable nodes and edges.
invariant: visited map/set prevents revisiting nodes; maps old node to new node for cloning.
failureModes: Not setting the clone in the map BEFORE recursing into neighbors (causes infinite loop on cycles).
Using node value as map key instead of node reference (fails with duplicate values).
contrastCases: Grid Flood Fill: cells in a grid; Graph Traversal: nodes with arbitrary adjacency.
DFS Cycle Detection: directed graph + three-color state; Graph Traversal: undirected reachability.
